content:
Over the past few days we have been studying the cloud of Numbers 9. We saw that the cloud protected Israel from the burning heat of the wilderness during the day, and at night it became a pillar of fire that gave light, warmth, and safety. Today we ask an important question: What is that fire for us as New Creation believers? We no longer see a visible pillar of fire, yet God has given us something even greater. He has given us His Word, His Spirit, and His Son, Jesus Christ. Together they provide the same light, warmth, guidance, and hope that the fire provided to Israel. The first purpose of the fire was to give light.

In the darkness of the wilderness, Israel could not see the path ahead. The fire made it possible to take the next step safely. In the same way, the Word of God gives us light when life becomes confusing. We do not always know what tomorrow will bring. We face decisions, difficulties, and unanswered questions. Yet God does not leave us in darkness. His Word gives us enough light for the next step. Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. Psalm 119:105

Notice that God does not always show us the entire journey. A lamp shines on the path directly ahead. In the same way, God often guides us one step at a time. When we open the Scriptures during a dark season, the Word becomes a fire that lights our path. Jeremiah 23:29 says, Is not My word like fire? The darker the night becomes, the more valuable the fire becomes. The more confused we feel, the more we need to draw near to God's Word.

The second purpose of the fire was to provide warmth. The desert nights were cold and harsh. The fire protected Israel from the cold. Spiritually, this speaks of the Holy Spirit. There are seasons when our hearts become cold because of disappointment, grief, suffering, or weariness. During those times, the Holy Spirit of God reminds us that we are loved by God and that we are not alone.

The love of God has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us - Romans 5:5; We are comforted because of God’s Holy Spirit dwelling in us as a Comforter. When life becomes difficult, we should not withdraw from God. Instead, we should draw closer through prayer, worship, fellowship, and the Word. The Spirit warms our hearts just as the fire warmed Israel during the long desert nights. The fire also reminds us of Christ Himself. Jesus said: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.” - John 8:12. Everything the fire was to Israel, Christ is to us. He is our light, our guide, and our example. When we do not know what to do, we look to Him. We study His life, His words, and His responses to suffering. He walked through rejection, pain, delay, and opposition, yet remained faithful to His Father. Hebrews 12:2 tells us:

Looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith.

The great lesson for the New Creation is that the cloud and fire have not disappeared. They have been fulfilled in Christ, the Spirit, and the Word.

We also have the cloud of witnesses spoken of in Hebrews 12:1. Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Daniel, Ruth, the apostles, and many others walked difficult paths before us. Their lives remind us that faith works and that God's promises are true. This gives us great joy because we are not walking alone. Others have faced darkness and reached the finish line through faith. It also gives us hope because God's presence has not left us. The world finds hope in changing circumstances, but believers find hope in the unchanging presence of God. Israel's confidence was not that the desert would become easier; their confidence was that the cloud would never leave them. Our confidence is not that every problem will disappear immediately, but that God will never leave us nor forsake us. “For God Himself has said, ‘I will never leave you nor forsake you.’” - Hebrews 13:5. As long as Christ is with us, there is light. As long as the Spirit is within us, there is warmth. As long as the Word is before us, there is direction. Therefore, let us stay close to the fire. Let us stay close to Christ, His Word, His Spirit, and the testimonies of those who have gone before us.

The closer we stay to the fire, the more light, warmth, joy, and hope we receive. The cloud is still above us, the fire is still among us, and our eternal home is still ahead of us.

title: Prayer
text: Father God, thank You for giving us Your Word, Your Spirit, and Your Son to guide us through every season of life. When we face darkness, let Your Word be our light. When our hearts grow cold, let Your Spirit warm and strengthen us. Help us keep our eyes fixed on Christ and follow Him faithfully. Fill us with joy, hope, and confidence, knowing that You will never leave us nor forsake us. Keep us close to the fire until the day we reach our eternal Home. In Christ's name, Amen.
